title: Hierarchical Context Distillation for Multi-Agent Multimodal Workflows
research_question: Can a hierarchical context-distillation layer that compresses intermediate multimodal evidence into role-specific summaries reduce coordination overhead and improve end-task accuracy in multi-agent multimodal reasoning workflows compared with standard full-context message passing?
hypothesis: In multi-agent multimodal reasoning systems, much of the failure and inefficiency comes from overconfident use of a single evolving context representation. A hierarchical distillation mechanism that preserves multiple plausible evidence summaries for different agent roles will improve accuracy-cost tradeoffs by reducing irrelevant context transfer while retaining uncertainty about competing interpretations.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around uncertainty-aware scheduling, adaptive decomposition, escalation, and evidence routing in agentic workflows, suggesting a crowded space around routing and replanning but an unaddressed gap around representation of shared context itself. The self-adaptive systems literature in the KB explicitly highlights model-selection uncertainty and argues that relying on a single best model can create overconfident decisions; this principle appears transferable to multi-agent AI workflows, where agents often exchange one long shared trace or one chosen interpretation. A promising new direction is therefore to optimize the workflow by distilling multimodal context into compact, role-specific, uncertainty-preserving summaries before coordination, targeting the root cause of communication overhead and brittle collaboration rather than proposing another scheduler or routing heuristic.
